parameters.name: Procore-Company-Id
parameters.description: Unique company identifier associated with the Procore User Account.

parameters.name: budget_view_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the Budget View (also known as Budget Template).

get.summary: Get Summary Rows for a Project's Budget
get.description:
Get summary rows for a project's budget view. Rows are grouped and aggregated according to `group_by`, unlike Detail Rows, which returns one row per budget line item.
To restrict or reorder which columns are returned, pass `column_ids` with the desired column `id` values, in the desired order. A column's `id` (used for `column_ids`) is different from its `attribute` (the key used for that column's value in each row below) — see [Get a Budget View](https://developers.procore.com/reference/rest/budget-view?version=latest) for the `columns` array, which has both plus display metadata (`label`, `type`, `format`, `display_rules`).
To read rows from a snapshot instead of the live budget, pass `source_snapshot_id` — this query parameter is shared across this endpoint, Detail Rows, and the Budget View endpoint.
This endpoint is paginated with `page`/`per_page` (maximum 100); requests with a larger `per_page` return 400. Page through results with `page`, and read `Total`, `Per-Page`, and `Link` from the response headers.

id.description: ID of the filter. Required for segment and attribute filters.

tier.description: Tier of the Segment if applicable

parameters.name: group_by
parameters.description:
Array of group objects to create hierarchical groupings. Rows will be grouped by the first criterion, 
then by the second within each first-level group, and so on.

Supported group object types:
  - WBS segment group
    Structure:
      - id: <segment_id>
      - tier: <segment_tier>
      - type: 'segment'
      - values: <array of segment item ids>

    Example:
    `{"id": "23", tier: <segment_tier>, "type": "segment", "values": [2, 3]}`
    
  - WBS attribute group
    Structure:
      - id: <attribute_id>
      - type: 'attribute'
      - values: <array of attribute item ids>

    Example:
    `{"id": "23", "type": "attribute", "values": [2, 3]}`

**Hierarchical grouping examples**:

Multiple groups (array format):
```json
[
  {"id": "12", "tier": 1, "type": "segment"},
  {"id": "23", "type": "attribute"}
]
```

Query string example:
`group_by[0][id]=12&group_by[0][tier]=1&group_by[0][type]=segment&group_by[1][id]=23&group_by[1][type]=attribute`

This would group rows first by segment ID 12, then by attribute ID 23 within each segment group.

tier.description: Tier of the Segment if applicable

schema.description: Array of group objects for hierarchical grouping

parameters.name: comparison
parameters.description:
Specifies what snapshot and budget view columns to compare against, as well as what comparison columns to include in the response.
Supported object 
  - Structure:
      - snapshot_id: number
      - column_ids: array of numbers
      - modes: array of string enums
        - comparison
        - variance

    Example:
    `{"snapshot_id": "23", "column_ids": ["1", "2"], "modes": ["variance"]}`

    Query string example:
    `comparison[snapshot_id]=1&comparison[column_ids][]=23&comparison[column_ids][]=45&comparison[modes][]=variance`

snapshot_id.description: ID of the snapshot to compare against

column_ids.description: List of column IDs to include in the comparison

modes.description: The comparison modes to include with reference column values

parameters.name: column_ids
parameters.description: Array of Column IDs ordered by desired position.

parameters.name: source_snapshot_id
parameters.description:
Unique identifier for a budget snapshot.
If provided, the response reflects that snapshot instead of the live budget.
If omitted, the response reflects the live budget.

This single query parameter is shared across the Budget View, Detail Rows, and
Summary Rows v2.0 endpoints.

parameters.name: filter_groups
parameters.description:
Alternative to `filters` for expressing OR logic. An array of filter groups: groups are OR'd together,
while the filters within each group are AND'd. Each inner element has the same shape as a `filters` entry.

Per-Page.description: Number of items retrieved per page

Total.description: Total number of items to be retrieved

Link.description: Link headers for the first, prev, next, and last link

currency_iso_code.description: Currency iso code for all summary rows

groups.description: Array of group objects containing label and value pairs. Each element represents a level in the grouping hierarchy.

value.description: Array of IDs for the group items. When multiple entities share the same group name, all their IDs are included in this array.

budget_forecast.description: Sum of all budget forecast in the group. Omitted when `column_ids` is provided and the Forecast To Complete column is not among the requested columns.

advanced_forecasting.description: Advanced forecasting columns (only present when budget view role is forecasting). Contains spread columns, dates, curve, and forecast remainder.

forecast_remainder.description: Remaining forecast amount not allocated to spread periods

spread_{month}_{year}.description: Spread amount for a specific month/year period. The actual keys will vary based on the forecast period range (e.g., spread_january_2025, spread_february_2025).

__attribute_key_from_columns_api__.description:
Placeholder name for a dynamic key: this literal string is never returned. There is one additional key like this per visible source or formula column in this budget view, and each one's real name is that column's `attribute` value.
To resolve these keys, call [Get a Budget View](https://developers.procore.com/reference/rest/budget-view?version=latest#get-a-budget-view) for this row's `budget_view_id` and read its `columns` array. Each entry's `attribute` field is the literal key this row object uses for that column's value; its `label`, `type`, `format`, and `display_rules` describe how to interpret it. For a standard column (`type: standard`), `attribute` is a fixed semantic name, e.g. `approved_budget_changes`; for a source or formula column (`type: source` or `type: formula`), `attribute` is always `column_{id}`, e.g. `column_4521`.

reference.description: Row value for the column in the reference view

comparison.description: Row value for the column in the comparison view

variance.description: Variance between the reference and comparison values

import http.client

conn.request("GET", "/rest/v2.0/companies/%7Bcompany_id%7D/projects/%7Bproject_id%7D/budget_views/%7Bbudget_view_id%7D/summary_rows?page=SOME_INTEGER_VALUE&per_page=SOME_INTEGER_VALUE&filters=SOME_ARRAY_VALUE&group_by=%5Bobject%20Object%5D&group_by=%5Bobject%20Object%5D&comparison=SOME_OBJECT_VALUE&column_ids=SOME_ARRAY_VALUE&source_snapshot_id=SOME_STRING_VALUE&filter_groups=SOME_ARRAY_VALUE")

print(data.decode("utf-8"))

x-changelog.description:
The `group_by` parameter now accepts an array of group objects to enable hierarchical grouping. 
This allows you to group budget rows by multiple criteria in a nested fashion, reducing the number 
of API requests needed for complex data retrieval scenarios. When using multiple group_bys, 
the `group_label` and `group_value` fields in the response will be arrays instead of single values.
